files.content:
# Topic Vulnerability

Static analysis of ELF files

# Theme

Enabling the discovery of the flag string through decompilation

# Expected solver's thought process

1. Perform static analysis with Ghidra or GDB.
2. Confirm that the flag string is provided in an array.

# Expected Difficulty

Easy

# Reference Materials

https://wiki.dlang.org/LDC_inline_assembly_expressions

# This file represents the base specification of your challenge. It is used by
# other tools to install and deploy your challenge.

# NOTE: Please edit from here
#
# Parts that need to be edited have the TODO: prefix.
############################

author: "JUCK"           # TODO: Please set your name.
category: "reversing"          # TODO: Please set the category. Add one of web/crypto/misc/pwnable/reversing/welcome.
description: |
    After C language, this is the one!
    
    This is the next trending programming language!

    * `libgphobos5` is required in some environments.
    Also, use `echo -n` as necessary.

    Note: In some environments, `libgphobos5` is required.
    Also, use the `echo -n` command as necessary.

flags:
     - "ctf4b{N3xt_Tr3nd_D_1an9uag3_101}"

# Accepts strings

     - author:JUCK             # TODO: Please set the author. Include author:.
     - easy      # TODO: Please add the difficulty. Add one of beginner/easy/medium/hard.

# Provide paths to files from the same directory that this file is in
# Accepts strings
files:
    - d-compile.zip

############################

    decay: 225
    minimum: 100

state: visible

# Specifies what version of the challenge specification was used.
# Subject to change until ctfcli v1.0.0
version: "0.1"

1. Submit to a decompilation tool (GDB in this case).
2. Looking at `main`, `_Dmain` is called, so check its content.
3. Looking at 0x3382 and beyond, it can be seen that an array starting with 0x63, 0x74, ... is being created.
